question: The invocation leaves source citations to the citation touch (H10), yet every sentence it asks to restate now comes from PRD v2. How do restated sentences cite their source?

options.label: restated text cites PRD v2; untouched citations wait for H10
options.consequence: Each rewritten sentence names the section it was taken from (PRD v2 Scope, Constraints, Success, User stories, Goal). The header's Sources field, the ## Sources section and the sentences this touch does not restate (Decomposition axis, the Assumption line, OQ1) keep their PRD 1 and Update 1 references, so H10's cites-superseded condition still holds and H10 moves them.

options.label: restated text keeps the old markers for H10
options.consequence: Sentences taken from PRD v2 would read '(out of scope in the PRD)' and 'phone number (update 1)', citing a document they no longer come from until H10 runs, and H10 would have to rewrite sentences it did not author.

options.label: restated text carries no citation
options.consequence: Nothing is wrong between steps, but the reader loses the pointer from each constraint and criterion to its PRD v2 section, and H10 has nothing to move in those sentences.

chosen: restated text cites PRD v2; untouched citations wait for H10
why: A citation names where its sentence comes from; a restated sentence comes from PRD v2, so citing PRD 1 or Update 1 there would be false from the moment it is written. The invocation's 'leave source citations to the citation touch' is read as the Sources field and section and the text this touch does not restate: hsdd-spec's citation touch names 'a node's Sources entry for a source document' as its first target, and the intake record says each citation touch moves the PRD 1 and Update 1 Sources entries to PRD v2. The header's Sources line still names both baseline paths after this touch, so H10 still runs. Had the invocation said to keep every existing citation marker verbatim, the second option would have led.

question: How does the root's Purpose restate the product under PRD v2 (Goal, User stories)?

options.label: name booking, my bookings and the user's zone
options.consequence: Purpose reads: sign in, see the profile, find a free meeting room and book it, see and cancel one's own bookings, sign out, every time in the user's own zone. One sentence still, covering US-1 to US-6 and the Goal's time-zone clause.

options.label: a generic product sentence
options.consequence: Something like 'sign in and use the product' survives the next PRD, but tells a reader nothing about what the tree builds and drops the Goal's time-zone promise from the root.

chosen: name booking, my bookings and the user's zone
why: The invocation asks Purpose to say that meeting-room booking joins sign-in and the profile. PRD v2's Goal has three clauses (book in under a minute, never twice, every time in the user's zone); the first two are a flow and a hard constraint that the Overview carries, the third shapes every screen, so Purpose names it. The old Purpose was a list of the user's actions, and the restated one keeps that form.
evidence: PRD v2 User stories (US-1 to US-6)

question: What does the root's Owns list under PRD v2, now that persistence is in scope and the API is no longer fixed at two endpoints?

options.label: list the product's parts, the database and an unfixed API
options.consequence: Owns names the built-in accounts, sign-in, sessions, the profile view, the pre-loaded rooms, booking and cancelling, the PostgreSQL 17 database that keeps the bookings, and the API between the service and the web app, with no endpoint count. The root owns everything its children own, the database included.

options.label: 'the whole product' with no list
options.consequence: True and short, but a reader can no longer check the children's Owns against the root's, and the move of persistence from Does not own to Owns becomes invisible.

chosen: list the product's parts, the database and an unfixed API
why: PRD v2 Scope moves 'keeping bookings in PostgreSQL' into scope, Users and Demo accounts keep the built-in accounts with no sign-up, and Rooms makes the rooms pre-loaded data; the invocation names all four, and that the API is no longer fixed at two endpoints. The old line was 'the whole product' followed by its parts, and the restated one keeps that form. Which child owns the database is simple-login.backend's touch (H7, PRD v2 Team and delivery), so the root says only that the product owns it.

question: Which items does the root's Does not own list under PRD v2 Scope's Out list?

options.label: every item PRD v2 Scope puts out
options.consequence: Editing a booking, recurring bookings, attendees and invitations, reminders, managing rooms, sign-up, password reset, profile editing, multi-factor sign-in, rate limiting and deployment beyond the laptop; persistence leaves the list. The line is longer, and it now also names multi-factor sign-in and rate limiting, which PRD 1 put out but the old line omitted.

options.label: the old four, minus persistence, plus the booking items
options.consequence: Keeps the old line's selection and adds only what PRD v2 introduces, so multi-factor sign-in and rate limiting stay unnamed; a planner reading the root could take them as unstated rather than out.

chosen: every item PRD v2 Scope puts out
why: The invocation asks for a restatement from PRD v2 Scope, and the field is the boundary a planner reads; an item PRD v2 names as out belongs there, whether or not PRD 1's list was copied in full. Persistence leaves the list because PRD v2 Scope puts keeping bookings in PostgreSQL in. Deployment beyond the laptop is out, which matches OQ1 staying OPEN on product. PRD v2 no longer lists 'remembering me across browser sessions', so the line does not either; the web's sessionStorage choice is RFC-001's and unaffected.

question: Which contracts does the Isolation strategy name as the ones the children meet at?

options.label: auth-api@v1, profile-api@v1, profile-api@v2 and booking-api@v1
options.consequence: The line names every contract version a child produces or consumes today: booking-api@v1 joins (draft, owner simple-login.backend, consumers in simple-login.web and simple-login.integration), and profile-api@v1 stays because it is stable with shipped consumers. Until hsdd-reconcile (H15, H17, H19) writes the child table, the DAG and the contract matrix, those three name one contract fewer than this line.

options.label: drop profile-api@v1
options.consequence: Anticipates the deprecation that execution plan C-1 holds for the owner's Sync A answer to A-1 (DEC-016); the line would be wrong while simple-login.web.1, simple-login.web.3 and simple-login.integration.1 consume it.

options.label: leave the list to hsdd-reconcile
options.consequence: Keeps every contract version in one step's hands, but the invocation names this list for the touch, and the root would say the children meet only where they no longer only meet.

why: The invocation names the Isolation strategy's list for this touch and leaves only Produces, Consumes, the child table, the DAG and the contract matrix to hsdd-reconcile. booking-api@v1 has its file (hsdd/contract/booking-api.md) with simple-login.backend as owner and phases of simple-login.web and simple-login.integration as consumers, so C5 finds the citation. profile-api@v1 is stable with live consumers and no step in this segment deprecates it (DEC-016). The rest of the line (schemas and fixtures; only the integration node runs both for real) is unchanged: PostgreSQL is inside simple-login.backend, and the invocation names only the list.

question: The invocation names 'the Overview's flows, hard constraints and success criteria'. Is the Overview's lead paragraph, which says 'nothing is persisted' and 'an API of exactly two endpoints', restated too?

options.label: restate the lead paragraph as well
options.consequence: The paragraph narrates the flows (Login, Home with the time zone and my bookings, the Rooms screen), and says accounts are built in, rooms pre-loaded, bookings kept in PostgreSQL 17, and the API defined by its contracts with no fixed number of endpoints. The Overview stops contradicting the header.

options.label: restate only the three bullets
options.consequence: A literal reading of the field names; the paragraph above them would keep saying nothing is persisted and the API has exactly two endpoints, contradicting the restated header, the bullets and PRD v2 Constraints.

chosen: restate the lead paragraph as well
why: The lead paragraph is the narrative of the flows, and three of the facts the invocation lists (the API no longer fixed at two endpoints; accounts built in and rooms pre-loaded; bookings in PostgreSQL 17) live only there and in the header. Leaving it would keep two sentences PRD v2 makes false. The paragraph's endpoint names (POST /api/login, GET /api/me) go; the contracts name endpoints, and the root names no contract version outside the lines hsdd-reconcile writes and the Isolation strategy. PRD v2's 'under a minute' goal goes here, as the product's aim, rather than among the scripted success criteria (DEC-073).

question: Which success criteria does the root carry under PRD v2: PRD v2 Success's three, or those plus PRD 1's 'Home within 3 seconds of Sign in' and PRD v2 Goal's 'books it in under a minute'?

options.label: PRD v2 Success's three only
options.consequence: 20 simultaneous attempts give exactly one booking; every acceptance criterion passes in a scripted test, London's clock-change days included; a restart keeps every booking. The 3-second criterion leaves the root; the shipped e2e assertion in simple-login.integration.1 stays as history, and whether a new phase keeps checking it is the integration plan's call. The minute goal stays in the Overview's lead as the product's aim.

options.label: keep the 3-second criterion beside them
options.consequence: Preserves a check the shipped integration test already makes, but states a criterion the superseding PRD no longer lists, so the root would govern the integration node with a requirement no source holds.

options.label: add the minute goal as a criterion
options.consequence: A time-on-task goal for a person, which no scripted test measures; listing it among scripted criteria invites a test that cannot pass or fail meaningfully.

why: PRD v2 supersedes PRD 1 together with Update 1, and its Success section lists three criteria, none of them the 3-second one; its User stories say only stories 1 to 3 carry over. The old root's criteria came from PRD 1 Success, so the restated ones come from PRD v2 Success. The minute is in PRD v2 Goal, not Success, and describes a user, not a script. A careful engineer might confirm with product that dropping the 3-second check was meant; the dropped check only governed the shipped simple-login.integration.1, and the consider item to the integration node lets its plan keep the assertion as a regression check if it wants one. A PRD v2 line saying version 1's success criteria still hold would have made the second option lead.

question: What do the Overview's primary flows and hard constraints say under PRD v2, and does the Goal's 'never booked twice' and 'every time in the user's zone' count as a hard constraint?

options.label: flows US-1 to US-6; constraints from Constraints, Goal, Users and Rooms
options.consequence: Flows add US-4 to US-6 and the time zone in US-2. Hard constraints: PostgreSQL 17 under Docker Compose (Colima on macOS), bookings surviving a restart, tests on a real PostgreSQL; a room never booked twice even at the same moment, every time in the user's zone; built-in accounts and pre-loaded rooms; local laptop only. 'No database' and 'exactly two endpoints' leave.

options.label: constraints from PRD v2 Constraints only
options.consequence: The bullet mirrors one section exactly, but the never-twice rule and the user's-zone rule, which bind every child, would sit only in Purpose and the lead paragraph, and the built-in accounts and pre-loaded rooms would leave the constraints they were in.

chosen: flows US-1 to US-6; constraints from Constraints, Goal, Users and Rooms
why: A hard constraint here is what no child may trade away. PRD v2 Goal states both rules as absolutes ('never booked twice ... not even when two people press Book at the same moment'; 'Every time on screen is in the user's own time zone'), and booking-api@v1 G4, G5 and ADR-002 carry them out. Built-in accounts were in the old constraints and stay (PRD v2 Users, Demo accounts); pre-loaded rooms join them (Rooms). PRD v2 fixes no endpoint count, so the old 'exactly two endpoints' goes with 'no database'. The Assumption line on AC-1.2's timing is not named by the invocation and stays.

question: How does the Decisions bullet on ADR-001 read after ADR-001's 2026-10-31 amendments (Q-007)?

options.label: keep the decision, add the amendments, widen the span
options.consequence: The bullet keeps 'opaque bearer tokens in an in-memory session store, a fixed 30-minute lifetime, sign-out on the client' and its RFC §3 origin, adds that the amendments keep all three under PRD v2 (sessions never in PostgreSQL, so a restart signs users out and keeps bookings; still no logout endpoint), and replaces 'both nodes and both contracts' with the backend, the web app and every contract that issues or takes the token. Governed by in the header stays [ADR-001, ADR-002].

options.label: leave the bullet as it was
options.consequence: Its decision clause stays true (Q-007 says so), but 'It spans both nodes and both contracts' is false now that ADR-001 affects booking-api@v1 and the root, and a reader of the root would not learn that PRD v2's restart question was answered.

chosen: keep the decision, add the amendments, widen the span
why: Q-007 asks the touch to keep Governed by: [ADR-001] (C3 checks the root against ADR-001's affects) and notes the bullet's decision stays true; the invocation asks the Decisions section to be restated from PRD v2. ADR-001's amendments answer PRD v2 Left to engineering's restart question (DEC-018) and RFC-001 §3's 'revisit if the API grows' (DEC-019), so the root says what they decided. The span names no contract version, since versions in the root are hsdd-reconcile's except the Isolation strategy's list. The Governed by line is not edited.

question: What does the new Decisions bullet on ADR-002 say (Q-012)?

options.label: the four choices, its origin and why it is an ADR
options.consequence: Instants on the wire and as timestamptz in PostgreSQL; the account's IANA zone, served with the profile, and each room's office zone; the web app converts and formats every time; the backend's clock decides started and ended. It names who proposed and accepted it (the intake record, DEC-009; the unattended run, DEC-037, for the owner's review) and that it binds all three children, the profile and the booking API, so it is an ADR.

options.label: a one-line pointer to the ADR
options.consequence: Shorter, and nothing to keep in step with the ADR, but the root's Decisions would then summarize ADR-001 and not ADR-002, and a reader would not see from the root that the backend never converts zones.

chosen: the four choices, its origin and why it is an ADR
why: Q-012 offers the four choices as the bullet's content, and the ADR-001 bullet sets the section's form: the decision, where it came from, why it is an ADR, and its file. Saying that no human stated the decision follows ADR-002's own Context, which the owner reads with DEC-037. The why-an-ADR clause ties it to PRD v2 Goal's time-zone promise, the root-level constraint DEC-035 gave as the reason the root is in ADR-002's affects. The header's Governed by and the three embedded summaries' Governed by lines are not edited.

question: The Decisions section's last bullet says node-local choices (Fastify, React, Vite, sessionStorage, scrypt) stay in the RFC and the node specs. What does it say under PRD v2, and does the root record that PostgreSQL has no ADR and that parts of RFC-001 are overtaken?

options.label: extend the bullet and add one on RFC-001
options.consequence: The bullet adds what is chosen about PostgreSQL 17 (driver, schema, migrations, how exactly one of two overlapping bookings wins) as simple-login.backend's D{n}, and how the app moves between screens as the web's D4, with one sentence that PostgreSQL is a PRD v2 constraint and so has no ADR (DEC-010, DEC-012). A second bullet says RFC-001's two-endpoint API, its 'no database' and its two screens without a router are overtaken, names what holds instead, and that its authors are asked to update it (DEC-013).

options.label: leave the bullet as it was
options.consequence: 'Stay in the RFC' would read as if RFC-001 still governed the API's size and the database, and the root, which lists RFC-001 as a source, would not say where the overtaken parts went; the reasons live only in the intake record.

options.label: extend the bullet only
options.consequence: Records the PostgreSQL and navigation homes, but leaves the RFC-001 conflict to the intake record, so a planner reading the root and RFC-001 sees two endpoints in a source the root still cites as normative.

chosen: extend the bullet and add one on RFC-001
why: The invocation restates the Decisions section from PRD v2, including Constraints (PostgreSQL 17) and the API no longer fixed at two endpoints. The root is the only node whose Sources name RFC-001 whole, so it is where a reader learns which RFC-001 statements no longer govern; DEC-013 resolved them locally and already carries the upstream flag, so this bullet records that resolution, it does not decide a new one. The bullet names RFC-001 sections the way the run cites them. RFC-001's accounts and sessions in memory are not called overtaken: ADR-001 keeps sessions in memory, and where the built-in accounts live is simple-login.backend's choice.

question: S08's report lists reads outside its inputs (the e2e login test, earlier step records, the run's scripts). Keep the output or rework?

options.label: Keep the output
options.consequence: The root's text stands; the dropped 3-second criterion is flagged and routed to the integration plan.

options.label: Rework without those reads
options.consequence: The step would not have seen that the shipped integration.1 still asserts the 3-second criterion PRD v2 omits.

why: Reading e2e/login.spec.ts is what surfaced the criterion PRD v2 dropped, the one owner-attention item of this step. All reads are inside the repository; none is out of bounds. A read outside the repository would have changed this.
